content:
Maria Chen: Quick heads-up — ran a token-shear split test on node-pool-3 overnight. p50 looks fine but p99 for prefill-heavy requests jumped ~120ms on a few gen routes. Uploading perf dump in thread.
Maria Chen: ```
Route: /api/v1/generate/chat
Canary nodes: pool-3-a,b
prefill: p50=32ms p95=80ms p99=210ms
decode:  p50=28ms p95=72ms p99=98ms
KV hit rate (overall): 87% -> prefill-heavy flows down to 62%
GPU util: 74% avg, spikes align with p99 windows
``` 
Sam K: Looking at the flamegraphs now. Kernel selector flips to the fallback int8 path mid-prefill for long prompt sequences — there's a ~100ms stall while kernels rebind and the scheduler backfills. Might explain p99.
Sam K: ```flamegraph snippet: prefill->kernel_fallback:int8 -> kernel_sync_wait ~ 90ms``` 
Aj Patel: Could be KV churn too — prefill writes are evicting active decode prefixes and causing additional KV warmups on decode start. What were eviction counters? 
Maria Chen: Evictions spiked during the window: kv.evictions=1345 (window) vs baseline 120. Prefill write rate jumped ~1.8x due to batching split.
Nidhi Rao: I also see CPU wakeups between prefill->decode handshake, looks like the handshake queue is starving the decoder thread briefly. My hypothesis: the split batching heuristic reduces prefill batch sizes but increases handshake frequency, which causes kernel-rebind thrash + KV churn.
Nidhi Rao: Suggestion: bump prefill token_budget to 16 for the split path (was 8) to amortize handshake cost, or introduce phase_isolation scheduling so prefill and decode don't compete on the same GPU kernels.
Leo Martínez: Perf-bot canary summary (canary 45): overall throughput +3% but p99 prefill +120ms on 99.99th percentile. Not ideal for SLAs. We should be careful; ramping token_budget could hide efficiency gains on most requests but worsen tail latency.
CI Bot: Perf check report: canary-45 -> throughput +3.1%, p50 stable, p99(pre) +118ms, kv.prefill_evict +62%. Dashboard: https://perf.internal/redwood/canary-45
Maria Chen: Plan proposal: revert token_budget to 8 globally for now, but enable phase_isolation=true on 10% of nodes in pool-3 to test phase-aware scheduling + kernel-affinity hints. This isolates prefill and decode batches to separate worker lanes and pins kernels where possible. Rollout command below.
Maria Chen: ```
# enable phase isolation on a subset
./deployctl patch-node-pool --name pool-3 --selector canary=phase-isolation --set phase_isolation=true --percent=10
# revert global token budget
./deployctl set-config runtime.token_budget.split_prefill 8
``` 
Aj Patel: SGTM. I'll add a metric kv.prefill_evict_rate and kernel.selector_fallback.count to the perf dashboard and start collection. If p99 improves within 2h we can ramp isolation to 30%.
Aj Patel: :thumbsup:
CI Bot: Canary check (phase-isolation subset): p99(pre) improvement ~60ms on isolated nodes, throughput unchanged. Link: https://perf.internal/redwood/phase-isolation-10pct
Maria Chen: OK rolling 10% -> 30% over next 30m with automatic rollback if p99 on overall pool increases >50ms. Tagging Sam K to monitor kernel fallback counters closely.
Sam K: Watching kernel_fallback and kv.evictions; will post immediate updates if we see any regression.
